title: Augmentation of a quotient of Weyl alternants
statement:
Let $X,Y$ be finite-rank free abelian groups with a perfect integer pairing $\langle-,-angle:X	imes Y	o\mathbf Z$. Let $\Phi\subset X\setminus\{0\}$ be a finite spanning set of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, with bijectively indexed coroots $\alpha^\vee\in Y$ spanning $Y\otimes\mathbf Q$. Assume this is a reduced crystallographic root datum (with the integer root-pairing conventions of [lem-sfb-crystallographic-positive-base]): $\langle\alpha,\alpha^\veeangle=2$; the reflections $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha^\veeangle\alpha$ and the dual reflections preserve the roots and corresponding coroots; and the only scalar multiples of a root that are roots are itself and its negative. Fix a positive system $\Phi^+$ with simple-root base $\Delta$, meaning every root has integer simple-root coordinates all nonnegative or all nonpositive, with $\Phi^+$ the former. Assume $ho=	frac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$ belongs to $X$. Let $W$ be the finite group generated by the reflections, and put $A(
u)=\sum_{w\in W}\det(w)e^{w
u}$ in the group algebra $\mathbf Q[X]$, with $e^xe^y=e^{x+y}$ and determinant on $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. Let $\epsilon:\mathbf Q[X]	o\mathbf Q$ be augmentation, $\epsilon(\sum a_xe^x)=\sum a_x$. For $
u,\sigma\in X$ assume $\langle\sigma,\alpha^\veeangle
e0$ for every root, and let $q\in\mathbf Q[X]$ satisfy $qA(\sigma)=A(
u)$. Then
$$\epsilon(q)=\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+} rac{\langle
u,\alpha^\veeangle}{\langle\sigma,\alpha^\veeangle}.$$
Moreover $\langleho,\alpha^\veeangle$ is a positive integer for every positive root $\alpha$. The zero-rank root datum is included: its empty product is $1$. No existence of $q$ is assumed beyond the displayed polynomial identity.

source.place: Section 22d, p.480, antisymmetry operator before Theorem 22.50; abstract augmentation calculation supplied by the agent (see report). WANTED: Jantzen 2003, II.5.12, for the textbook Weyl-dimension specialization.

proof.text: First handle rank zero. Since the roots span $X\otimes\mathbf Q$, there are no roots and $X=Y=0$, $W=\{1\}$ and $A(\nu)=A(\sigma)=1$. The assumed identity forces $q=1$, so the conclusion is the empty product $1$ and positivity is vacuous. Henceforth write $V=X\otimes\mathbf Q$, $U=Y\otimes\mathbf Q$ and $r=\dim V>0$; the pairing extends to a perfect rational pairing. Put $N=|\Phi^+|$, $D(v)=\prod_{\alpha>0}\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ and $B(h)=\prod_{\alpha>0}\langle\alpha,h\rangle$. These denote actual homogeneous polynomials, not just their values.

source.place: Section 22d, p.480, antisymmetry operator; agent augmentation calculation

proof.text: Fix a simple root $\delta$. If $\beta>0$ and $\beta\ne\delta$, some simple coordinate of $\beta$ other than its $\delta$ coordinate is positive: otherwise reducedness would force $\beta=\delta$. Reflection in $\delta$ leaves that coordinate unchanged. Since every root has coordinates of one sign, $s_\delta\beta$ is positive. As $s_\delta$ is an involution and $s_\delta\delta=-\delta$, it therefore permutes $\Phi^+\setminus\{\delta\}$. Summing gives $s_\delta\rho=\rho-\delta$. Comparing with $s_\delta\rho=\rho-\langle\rho,\delta^\vee\rangle\delta$ and using $\delta\ne0$ proves $\langle\rho,\delta^\vee\rangle=1$.

source.place: Appendix C.21--C.22, p.612: base and positive-root coordinates; explicit simple-reflection calculation

proof.text: Choose a rational basis of $V$ and its coordinate dot product $b_0$. The finite sum $b(v,u)=\sum_{w\in W}b_0(wv,wu)$ is rational, symmetric, $W$-invariant by reindexing, and positive definite after extension to $\mathbf R$, since the identity summand is positive on every nonzero vector. Orthogonality of $s_\alpha$, applied to its fixed hyperplane and its $-1$ eigenvector $\alpha$, gives $\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle=2b(v,\alpha)/b(\alpha,\alpha)$. Explicitly, pair $s_\alpha v=v-\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ with $s_\alpha\alpha=-\alpha$ and compare with $b(v,\alpha)$. The preceding step implies $b(\rho,\delta)=b(\delta,\delta)/2>0$ for each simple root. For $\alpha=\sum_\delta n_\delta\delta>0$, all $n_\delta\geq0$ and at least one is positive. Thus $b(\rho,\alpha)>0$, and the displayed formula proves $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle>0$. It is an integer because $\rho\in X$ and $\alpha^\vee\in Y$. The same formula shows that proportional coroot functionals correspond to proportional roots, so the linear factors of $D$ are pairwise nonproportional by reducedness.

source.place: Appendix C.19--C.21, pp.611--612: averaging and coroot formula, with the positivity argument written out

proof.text: We need the sign of $B$ under the dual $W$-action, defined by $\langle v,wh\rangle=\langle w^{-1}v,h\rangle$. For a root reflection $s=s_\gamma$, permutation of the root pairs $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ gives $B(sh)=cB(h)$ with $c\in\{1,-1\}$. Replace $\gamma$ by its positive representative and write $B=\ell_\gamma G$, where $\ell_\gamma(h)=\langle\gamma,h\rangle$. Since $\ell_\gamma(sh)=-\ell_\gamma(h)$, cancellation gives $G(sh)=-cG(h)$. Restrict to $H=\ker\ell_\gamma$, which $s$ fixes pointwise. Every remaining factor of $G$ restricts to a nonzero linear polynomial on $H$, because distinct positive roots are nonproportional. Their product is nonzero: the cited polynomial-ring statement gives a domain after choosing coordinates on $H$, including $\dim H=0$ (when $G=1$). Hence $(1+c)G|_H=0$ implies $c=-1=\det(s)$. Multiplication along any word of root reflections now gives $B(wh)=\det(w)B(h)$.

source.place: Appendix C.15 and C.18, p.611: reflection generators and reducedness; agent discriminant-sign calculation

proof.text:
Choose a basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of $U$, algebraically independent variables $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, the field $K=\mathbf Q(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$, and $h=\sum_i z_i u_i\in U\otimes K$. Then $B(h)\ne0$, since each root gives a nonzero linear polynomial in the independent variables and their polynomial ring is a domain. For each $j\geq0$ define the homogeneous polynomial on $V\otimes K$
$$F_j(v)=\frac1{j!}\sum_{w\in W}\det(w)\langle wv,h\rangle^j.$$
Reindexing $w$ by $ws_\alpha$ shows $F_j(s_\alpha v)=-F_j(v)$. Therefore $F_j$ vanishes on the fixed hyperplane $\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$, since $K$ has characteristic zero. Apply the cited hyperplane-divisibility statement over the infinite field $K$ to the $N$ distinct linear factors of $D$, whose nonproportionality was checked above. It gives $F_j=0$ for $j<N$ and $F_N=cD$ for a scalar $c\in K$.

source.place: Section 22d, p.480, antisymmetry operator; agent augmentation calculation

proof.text:
The scalar $c$ is nonzero; this must be checked rather than inferred from alternation. For a vector $a\in V$, let $\partial_a$ be the directional derivative on coordinate polynomials, defined by differentiating each monomial. Apply $T=\prod_{\alpha>0}\partial_\alpha$ to $F_N$. Repeatedly using $\partial_a\langle v',h\rangle^j=j\langle a,h\rangle\langle v',h\rangle^{j-1}$ (with $v'=wv$, so $a$ is replaced by $wa$), the factorial cancels and
$$TF_N=\sum_w\det(w)\prod_{\alpha>0}\langle w\alpha,h\rangle=\sum_w\det(w)B(w^{-1}h)=|W|B(h)\ne0.$$
Here the last equality is the sign calculation above and $\det(w)^2=1$. Since $F_N=cD$, the left side is $c(TD)$; $TD$ is a scalar because $D$ has degree $N$. Its nonzero right side proves $c\ne0$ without needing to compute $TD$.

source.place: Section 22d, p.480, antisymmetry operator; agent augmentation calculation

proof.text:
Define a $\mathbf Q$-algebra map $E:\mathbf Q[X]\to K[[t]]$ on the group-algebra basis by
$$E(e^x)=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{\langle x,h\rangle^j}{j!}t^j.$$
It respects multiplication because the coefficient of $t^j$ in $E(e^x)E(e^y)$ is $\sum_{i=0}^j\langle x,h\rangle^i\langle y,h\rangle^{j-i}/(i!(j-i)!)=\langle x+y,h\rangle^j/j!$ by the binomial formula. Extend by finite $\mathbf Q$-linear sums; negative lattice exponents cause no issue, since the inverse basis element maps to the series for $-x$. Directly $[t^0]E(q)=\epsilon(q)$, and $[t^j]E(A(\lambda))=F_j(\lambda)$. Thus all degrees below $N$ of the latter series vanish and its degree-$N$ coefficient is $cD(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda\in X$.

source.place: Section 22d, p.480, antisymmetry operator; agent augmentation calculation

proof.text:
Apply $E$ to the given polynomial identity $qA(\sigma)=A(
u)$ and compare the coefficient of $t^N$. The convolution formula and the vanishing of all coefficients of $E(A(\sigma))$ in degrees below $N$ leave precisely
$$\epsilon(q)cD(\sigma)=cD(
u).$$
The hypothesis on $\sigma$ makes every factor of $D(\sigma)$ nonzero, and $c
e0$ was proved above. Cancel in the field $K$ to obtain $\epsilon(q)=D(
u)/D(\sigma)$. Both sides lie in $\mathbf Q$, whose map into $K$ is injective. Expanding the definitions of $D$ yields exactly the asserted product. No condition on $
u$ was used: if $
u$ is singular, $D(
u)=0$ and this same coefficient comparison gives augmentation zero. Together with the positivity and rank-zero arguments this proves every clause.
